page: Hetzner Cloud ccx23 is a general-purpose cloud instance powered by dedicated AMD EPYC x86_64 processors running under the QEMU hypervisor. The virtual machine provides 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz, supported by 32 MB of L3 cache. Memory capacity is configured at 16.0 GB of RAM, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 3.91 GB per core. The server includes 160 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, contains zero GPUs, and includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses by default.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-thread execution metrics paired with moderate multi-core scalability. The instance scores 1986.0 in Geekbench single-core and 2692.67 in stress-ng single-core tests, placing it in the top 25 percent. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression and text processing also register strong throughput. In contrast, multi-threaded metrics reflect the 4-vCPU hardware ceiling: Geekbench multi-core performance is average at 4602.0, while multi-core stress-ng, Clang software compilation, and PassMark database operations fall in the lower quartiles. Memory bandwidth is modest, delivering 36.09 GB/sec on uncached 256 MB reads and 27.85 GB/sec on large block writes.

The dedicated vCPU allocation provides predictable compute capacity without the noisy-neighbor variability of shared hardware, offering high resource stability for standard workloads. However, the modest core count and limited uncached memory throughput constrain execution speeds for heavy parallel compiling and high-demand LLM token generation. Hetzner Cloud ccx23 is suitable for mid-tier web serving, application backends, staging environments, asynchronous task workers, and small-to-medium databases that benefit from dedicated execution and direct local NVMe storage.
description: Hetzner Cloud ccx23 is a dedicated general-purpose instance featuring 4 dedicated AMD EPYC vCPUs across 2 physical cores at 2.0 GHz, 16.0 GB of RAM, and 160 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Operating on the x86_64 architecture with 32 MB of L3 cache, the system eliminates noisy-neighbor CPU contention. Benchmarks show strong single-threaded performance, with Geekbench single-core scoring 1986.0 and stress-ng single-core reaching 2692.67, both in the top quartile. Multi-core performance is moderate due to the 4-thread constraint, yielding 4602.0 in Geekbench multi-core. Data transfer achieves 27.85 GB/sec on large memory writes, while Redis throughput attains 4.05 million operations per second. The server does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses or hardware accelerators. The ccx23 is configured for production application hosting, background task processing, API gateways, and light relational database workloads that require guaranteed CPU time.
